title: Facilitating and interviewing
goal: In expert interviews and internal meetings, you ask questions at a calm pace, get the other person to talk more, and bring a conversation back to the original question when it drifts.

scenes.label: Listening sessions and 1-on-1s with clients or colleagues
Something else (summarizing, voicing opinions, and so on)

troubles.label: I speak too fast or stumble
troubles.cause: You speed up and stumble because nerves make your breath shallow, and you push out a long sentence in one go on that shallow breath.

troubles.label: My voice goes high or shakes when I am nervous
troubles.cause: Your voice goes high or shakes because your breath is shallow and your throat tenses.

troubles.label: My voice is flat and sounds unsure
troubles.cause: Your voice sounds flat and unsure because you try to finish in one breath without leaving a pause.

troubles.label: The other person does not say much after my question
troubles.cause: The other person says little because the pause after your question is short, and you often speak again before they start.

troubles.label: The talk drifts and I cannot bring it back
troubles.cause: You cannot bring the talk back because you have no set way to sum up what was said so far before returning to the question.

diagnosis_tail: So you start by practicing breath and pauses alone. Next you try it in internal meetings and 1-on-1s, and then use it in the real interviews and meetings. Practice reminders come {when}.
diagnosis_scenes: You want to use this in: {scenes}.

stages.name: Practice alone
stages.scene: Every morning, and before the real thing

kata.text: Five minutes before the real thing, put a hand on your belly and count ten long out-breaths
Before a meeting, say your first three sentences (today's purpose, what you want decided, your first question) out loud, breathing in through your nose at each comma or period
The day before a listening session, write what you want to ask as three questions, and rephrase each to start with "In what situation..." or "For example..."
When the other person finishes, repeat one of their words as is, and then say your part
When an "um" is about to come out, take a light breath in through your nose and use it as the pause
At the start of a meeting, say in one sentence what you want decided today

stages.name: The real thing
stages.scene: Expert interviews, client listening, running a meeting

kata.text: When you are introduced, do not start right away; wait three seconds and then begin
After a follow-up question, stay silent for three seconds until the other person starts to talk
When the talk drifts, sum up what was said so far in one sentence, and then go back to the original question

pass_rule: You pass a stage when at least two of its steps get a "Did it" on different days.
graduation_rule: You graduate when all three are true: you passed stage 3, your count in recording 1 or 2 is half of your first value or less, and one person around you says your speaking is easier to follow than before.

measures.label: Number of "um" and "uh"
measures.how: Once a week, record one minute on your phone on the same topic (for example, how you explain your work this week). Count the "um" and "uh" and enter the number. You pass when it is half of your first count.

measures.label: Share of time you spoke
measures.how: In a recording of an interview or 1-on-1, check what percent of the time you were talking. In a listening session, 30% or less is a good guide. If you have no recording this week, leave it blank.

measures.label: Seconds to read a fixed text
measures.how: Read the fixed text below aloud to the end, time it, and enter the seconds. Your first time is your own baseline. If you read too fast, a longer time counts as progress.

read_text: Before a meeting, first narrow today's purpose down to one thing. Next, write down what you want decided and settle your first question. Once the talk begins, listen to the other person to the end and check only the parts you did not understand, briefly. When the talk widens, sum up what has been said in one sentence and go back to the original question. At the end, say aloud what was decided and what happens next. In any setting, take your time, steady your breath, and keep the same pace. When the listener is calm, the speaker can talk with more ease. Your volume can be as usual. If you misread a word, just keep going without correcting it. Read all of this aloud, to the very end.

reasons.label: I forgot
reasons.next: From tomorrow, the reminder comes 15 minutes earlier (15 minutes before the scene)

reasons.label: I could not bring it up
reasons.next: If you cannot bring it up on another day too, you go back one stage

reasons.label: I tried it, but it did not fit
reasons.next: Tomorrow you get a different step from the same stage

reasons.label: There was no scene
reasons.next: Today does not count. Tomorrow only the practice-alone steps appear

messages.drop: You could not bring it up two days in a row, so you go back one stage (stage {n}).
messages.remaining: {k} more "Did it" (on a different step, on a different day) and {next}.

check_question: Has my speaking become easier to follow lately?
